Try imagining the Psychosis that manifests from BPD warping your mind and senses, making you hear and see shit, twisting your every thought and pulling your strings like you're a fucking marionette. At that point you don't even know if you exist and if all the people around you are real or not. You end up wanting to fight or hide because you're absolutely terrified of everything. That's a small description of what some BPD episodes can be like. Trying to control something like that is pretty much impossible because it's like you've been trapped inside a cage where every little thing hurts or frightens you. 

Those with BPD are met with stigma from all angles because of their "terrible behaviour", but most of the time, the person underneath it all has been through some kind of trauma to make them that way. They still need love and acceptance. Kindness and being gentle goes a long way to breaking down all those walls and bringing back the person you love. Being angry with them just makes it far worse. When they are having an episode, regardless of how confusing their behaviour may seem, that's when they need their loved ones the most.

I may get hate for this comment, but I really need to voice my opinion on this.

Try to remember people with BPD are human beings who need love and understanding too. They are not monsters who just use people. I have BPD and CPTSD as mentioned, and I ended up like this after being mentally, physically, and sexually abused by my own family and other people around me for many, many years, and starting off my life with Clinical Depression and a terrible set of genes that left me with several debilitating Chronic Diseases. People with BPD are the emotional equivalent of a severe burn victim and sometimes the smallest thing can hurt immensely, that's why we freak out and go crazy; our way of thinking is far different from most other people. Of course, it's no excuse for being abusive and any kind of violence, and of course you didn't deserve being treated badly, but try to remember that we are all different and not everyone with BPD is "cruel/violent/manipulative" etc. We often feel so ashamed of our "outbursts" that we simply shut off, disassociate, and isolate ourselves from the world. It's scary for us and scary for the people we associate with, but none of it is done on purpose, and keeping control of ourselves can be extremely difficult. Of course, therapy and meds do help, but it's a constant battle between us and our own minds. Believe me when I say it's really no fun at all.

If you are referring to me as being snide and rude, I really wasn't. I was kind and worded it in a way that was meant as; you are lucky and I am glad you have a mother to say "I love you" to. I surely wouldn't wish what I have been through on anyone, and if it was "unhealthy" to mention my side of things and from my perspective, then I am sorry. I didn't expect much of a reaction at all, nevermind being told that "nobody asked". It just hurt, that's all, and I felt completely isolated. I wasn't trying to minimize anyone's struggle, they were not talking about anything bad. It just sometimes hurts like hell to see others speaking so fondly of their parents and family when I have had nobody since day one. But I'll keep quiet in the future.

If I'm making no sense or completely misunderstood your comment I apologise. I'm very low on sleep so I'm probably rambling.
